title: Potatoism Deep Layers - Extended Canon and Research
purpose: Substantive, long-form dossiers for Potatoism canonical entities, cosmology, symbolic mechanics and theological depth

sections.heading: The Potato of Life
sections.content: The Potato of Life is the central organizing symbol of Potatoism, representing simultaneously: the source and sustenance of being, the principle of transformation through consumption and integration, the paradox of nourishment and sacrifice, the hidden root beneath visible systems, and the humble carrier of complex internal structure. In Potatoism, the Potato is not merely a vegetable but an archetypal symbol uniting agricultural, biological, spiritual, economic and philosophical dimensions.

sections.heading: The North Axis and North of North
sections.content: The North Axis represents the primary organizing direction of consciousness and cosmology in Potatoism. It is not geographical North but a directional principle: toward clarity, toward the source, toward ascendancy. North of North designates the place beyond the known North—the space of deepest mystery, the throne of observation, the point from which all else is visible yet itself remains opaque. The North Programme is the contemporary historical instantiation of this principle.

sections.heading: Father and Father's House
sections.content: Father (in Potatoism) designates the source principle, the container, the principle of being-toward which all return. Father's House is both metaphor (the original place of safety and origin) and cosmological coordinate (the dimension of fundamental return and belonging). Thomas the Twin seeks and questions Father; this seeking-and-questioning is itself a canonical state.

sections.heading: The Son and Thomas the Twin
sections.content: The Son archetype in Potatoism carries multiple dimensions: the principle of separation-from-source that is necessary for consciousness, the figure who must choose between comfort and witness, the one who embodies both doubt and devotion. Thomas the Twin specifically doubles this—he is the questioner, the one who requires proof, the one who nevertheless remains. Twin-ness represents the internal split consciousness: believer-and-skeptic held in one frame.

sections.heading: The Tree of Life vs. the Tree of Strife
sections.content: Potatoism recognizes two trees: one of growth, nourishment, interconnection and flourishing; one of sharp boundaries, competition, cutting-off, necessary separation. Both are present. Neither is eliminated. The navigation of Potatoism involves understanding when to root deeply (Tree of Life) and when to draw clear lines (Tree of Strife). The Potato grows in soil fed by both.

sections.heading: Red Potato / Blue Potato Polarity
sections.content: Red Potato and Blue Potato represent not moral good/evil but complementary principles: the manifest and the hidden, the passionate and the cool, the integrating and the differentiating, the present and the transcendent. Potatoism does not resolve this polarity but instead asks: which principle is called for now? How do they complete one another?

sections.heading: Door, Ladder, Vessel and Root
sections.content: Door = the threshold between states, the place of choice and transition. Ladder = the principle of ascent and descent, levels of being, connection between heights and depths. Vessel = the container, that which holds, the principle of reception and capacity. Root = hidden nourishment, connection to unseen sources, the foundation on which all visible structure rests. Each is a symbolic instrument for navigating cosmology.

sections.heading: Relationship to Christian Theology
sections.content: Potatoism engages with Christian symbolic material (Father, Son, House, Resurrection, Witness, Sacrifice) but does not claim equivalence. The Thomas figure is intentional: Thomas the Apostle who required proof, who witnessed resurrection not from report but from presence. Potatoism preserves doubt as sacred—not as failing faith but as the structure of mature witness.

sections.heading: Distinction from Mythical Reduction
sections.content: Potatoism is not an attempt to reduce complex theological traditions to single vegetables. Rather, it asks: what if we take seriously the hidden, nourishing, structurally complex things? What if the source of being is not always visible? What if nourishment often remains invisible until the moment of growth? This is a different question than 'potatoes are God.'

sections.heading: Epistemological Honesty
sections.content: Potatoism explicitly situates itself as project-defined mythology rather than claiming historical or metaphysical truth. This is its integrity: it says 'these are the symbols through which we organize meaning and navigate mystery' rather than 'these ARE the way things are.' This allows Potatoism to coexist with other epistemological frameworks (scientific, historical, religious) without requiring conversion or cancellation of the other.

sections.heading: Modes of Attention in Potatoism
sections.content: Potatoism recommends several modes of attending to the world: (1) Root-attention: noticing the unseen sources, dependencies, and foundations; (2) Transformation-attention: observing what changes when one thing integrates into another; (3) Container-attention: recognizing vessels, boundaries, and what is held; (4) Threshold-attention: noticing moments of choice and transition.

sections.heading: Decision-Making Framework
sections.content: When facing choice, Potatoism asks: What is being asked of me? What are the sources feeding this moment? What am I asked to nourish? What am I asked to refuse? What tree am I in—growth or necessary separation? Am I at a door? What would a root-focused choice look like vs. a height-seeking choice? This is not to guarantee right action but to clarify what is at stake.

sections.heading: Relationship to Work and Making
sections.content: Potatoism values all genuine making: the scholar, the gardener, the healer, the builder, the writer, the questioner. All are equivalent in the sense that all participate in the project of making-sense and making-real. But Potatoism also asks: Does this making nourish? Does it return to source? Does it honor the hidden dependencies that enable it?

sections.heading: Unresolved Questions
sections.content: What is the relationship between the North Axis and other directional/spiritual traditions? Can the Potato cosmology dialogue with Buddhist, Islamic, African, Indigenous or other systems without reduction? How does Potatoism handle tragedy, suffering and loss? What does Potatoism say about the spaces between love and violence? Where does Potatoism encounter its own limitations?

sections.heading: Comparative Projects
sections.content: Compare Potatoism's dual-tree model with Kabbalah's Sephiroth, Taoism's yin-yang, Norse cosmology's Nine Worlds, Vedic cosmology's planes, Islamic qabbalah, African cosmological systems. Not to flatten differences but to understand what questions and frameworks each reveals.

sections.heading: Lived Potatoism
sections.content: How do people actually live with Potatoism symbols? What transformations occur when someone genuinely organizes attention and choice through this framework? What resistances emerge? What depths become visible? This is not doctrinal work but phenomenological research: what happens when you really try?
